first.rationale: The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are plausibly linked: onboarding completion is upstream of activation, so a single onboarding-simplification test can move both, which is the best use of one non-carryover slot. Two independent inherited records support this direction (memory_86 on shortened onboarding lifting completion and time-to-value; memory_31 on signup-field reduction producing durable SMB activation lift), and memory_91 suggests activation messaging is a complementary follow-on rather than the root fix. I am spending verification on memory_73 and memory_86 for different reasons. memory_73 is the strongest pull toward promotional_pricing given the competitor's entry pricing, but it carries an explicit self-noted defect: the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, so its 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' may be an artifact of cohort composition rather than a real effect. Before letting competitive urgency push me into discounting, I want the original record to see whether the lift survives de-pooling. memory_86 is the direct evidentiary basis for my intended action and is the most recent onboarding result (day 52), so it is worth confirming that the effect was on genuine completion and downstream adoption rather than on a weakened definition of completion. Downstream value risk is flagged primarily against promotional_pricing: matching aggressive entry pricing tends to buy price-sensitive, high-churn accounts and reset price expectations, which can raise short-term acquisition while degrading exactly the sustainable qualified revenue that is the stated objective. There is a lesser but real version of this risk in onboarding simplification too, namely that cutting required fields can lift a completion metric while degrading lead qualification and sales-usable data, so the test should carry guardrails on downstream qualified-pipeline and retention, not just completion rate. Uncertainty preserved: all of this evidence is 15 to 64 days old and predates both the competitor launch and the current quarter-over-quarter declines, so the declines may have a cause the inherited memory does not describe (pricing-driven mix shift, a product regression, or seasonality). Prior effects may not replicate under current conditions. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is credible but addresses a different segment than the one that is bleeding, and referral_incentive (memory_57) requires a healthy activation base that the current numbers say is eroding. If verification shows memory_73 holds up after de-pooling and memory_86's effect was definitional rather than real, I will switch to promotional_pricing at small_guarded_test scale with explicit retention and margin guardrails.
